teaching_language: Fully English. This is a SINGLE-LANGUAGE programme, not one of unibz's trilingual degrees. The admission document states flatly 'The official teaching language is English' and the brochure 'At a glance' box says 'Courses will be taught in: English'. Every course in the published study plan (Growth Mindset with its Design Thinking and Prototyping and Algorithmic Thinking and Coding modules, Network Thinking and Agent-based Modeling, Economics for Management, Foundations of Entrepreneurship, Statistical Methods for Business Analysis, Entrepreneurial Finance and Venture Capital, Project Management, Social Entrepreneurship, Innovation Management, Family Business Management, Marketing B2B and Sales Management, Service Design, Research Coaching LAB, Startups Law and Industrial Law, Entrepreneurial Marketing, Market Research, People Management, Scaling-up, Digital Transformation, Management and Design, Project LAB - Startup, Project LAB - Corporate Innovation, Free Choice Courses and the Thesis) is delivered in English. There is NO Italian or German course in the curriculum, no Italian/German requirement at entry, none during the programme and none to graduate. unibz's own overview page confirms the pattern: 'Most of our master programmes are taught only in English, so a B2 level in English is needed.' The Study Guide's dedicated page for students of English-taught masters states that such a programme 'is entirely in English and does not include language requirements in other languages'. Italian and German courses remain available free of charge at the unibz Language Centre as an optional benefit, not an obligation. The start-up project submitted with the application may also be written in English ('You may write your document in English', NABC guidance document).
campus: TWO campuses are used by this single programme, which is unusual: the main Bozen-Bolzano city-centre campus (Universitätsplatz 1 - piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Faculty of Economics and Management) AND NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano (Bruno-Buozzi-Straße 1 / via Bruno Buozzi 1). The brochure 'At a glance' box lists 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano, NOI techpark Bozen-Bolzano', and the programme page states 'Classes take place at the Bozen-Bolzano campus and at NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano, one of the partners of this programme.' NOI Techpark is not merely a location here but a named programme partner. The first semester opens with an introductory session at the Bitz unibz fablab (https://bitzfablab.unibz.it), the university's maker space used for the prototyping component of the Growth Mindset course. Practical consequence for an incoming student: unlike the Master in Software Engineering (NOI Techpark only) or the economics bachelors (city centre only), a student on this programme should expect to move between the two sites during the week. Faculty Secretariat: Universitätsplatz 1, +39 0471 013000, schoolofeconomics@unibz.it. Advisory Service: Universitätsplatz 1, +39 0471 012100, apply@unibz.it.
degree_class: LM-77 — Scienze economico-aziendali (Economics and Business Administration), the Italian master class for business/management degrees. CONFIRMED (the research brief carried this as 'to be verified'): the brochure 'At a glance' box states 'Degree class: LM-77', the programme page repeats it, unibz publishes a dedicated grade-statistics page titled 'Grade Statistics LM-77 — Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation (LM-77)', and the admission document's simultaneous-enrolment clause uses this programme's own class as its worked example: 'the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-77/LM-77'. 120 ECTS over 2 years / four semesters. Credit structure totalling 120 CP: 1st year 61 CP (Growth Mindset 14, Network Thinking and Agent-based Modeling 2, Economics for Management 12, Foundations of Entrepreneurship 8, Statistical Methods for Business Analysis 6, one typical subject 6, two complementary subjects 5 + 6, Research Coaching LAB 2); 2nd year 59 CP (Startups Law and Industrial Law 8, one typical subject 6, two typical subjects 12, one Project LAB 6, Free Choice Courses 12, Thesis 15). Note the thesis is 15 CP here, materially smaller than the 24-36 CP thesis blocks of unibz's engineering masters — this programme spends the weight on project work instead.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered, running and heavily subscribed. The official programme page for 2026/27 carries the status line 'Courses will definetely be starting'. Confirmed empirically on three independent counts: (1) the Early Bird ranking list for a.y. 2026/27 was published and digitally signed, admitting 30 EU and 10 non-EU applicants; (2) the Late Application ranking list for a.y. 2026/27 was published and signed, admitting a further 18 EU applicants; (3) the programme is listed with the status '(Application possible)' on the university's Additional Application Session page for 18/08 - 04/09/2026. Classes start 28/09/2026. This is not one of the dormant programmes (contrast Wood Technology and Tourism Management, which appear on the site but are not recruiting).
is_new_programme: No — a long-established programme, not a 2026 launch and not a rename. unibz has published Study Manifestos for the 'MASTER IN ENTREPRENEURSHIP AND INNOVATION' under class LM-77 since at least 2015 (Manifest2015_WWS-LM-77-Unt-e-Inn_e.pdf), with further manifestos in 2016 and 2019, and the programme page reports that 'In the last years, our students and alumni co-founded more than 15 new companies' plus an annual entrepreneurial-ecosystem field trip whose past destinations (Silicon Valley, Lisbon, Berlin, Tallinn, New York, Iceland, Oslo, Toulouse) imply many years of operation. The current curriculum version is dated 2024 (the downloadable plan is 'Study-plan-Entrepeneurship-and-Innovation-2024.pdf'), and the NABC application guidance slide deck on the unibz site is from Open Day 2022 and is still the linked reference. Practical caution for a candidate: because the programme is old and the linked guidance material is several years old, third-party pages and older brochures may describe slightly different course names or credit splits than the current 2024 plan.
majors_tracks_study_plans: No majors, but TWO STREAMS chosen after enrolment — a genuine fork in the curriculum rather than a labelling exercise. 'At the beginning of the second semester, you choose the stream that better fits your aspirations and goals. Entrepreneurship is the stream for the students aiming at founding a new venture, while Innovation and Management is the stream for those students who aspire to work and make an impact in innovative firms.' The downloadable study-plan diagram labels the two columns ENTREPRENEURSHIP and INNOVATION MANAGEMENT (the brochure prose calls the second 'Innovation and Management' — the same stream under two spellings). The streams diverge at the paired electives: Entrepreneurial Finance and Venture Capital vs Project Management; Social Entrepreneurship vs Innovation Management; in year two Entrepreneurial Marketing vs Market Research, and Project LAB - Startup vs Project LAB - Corporate Innovation. The first semester is entirely mandatory 'to set up a common ground'. Personalisation on top of the streams: 1 elective from the activated list in year one, 2 in year two, plus 12 CP of Free Choice Courses (usable in either year, list republished annually by the Faculty). ATTENDANCE IS COMPULSORY (minimum 75% of lectures) in five components marked ** — Design Thinking and Prototyping, Network Thinking and Agent-based Modeling, Foundations of Entrepreneurship, Research Coaching LAB, and whichever Project LAB is chosen — which makes this a materially more presence-bound degree than most unibz masters and a poor fit for someone planning to work full time. The Faculty Council decides each year which of the four second-year 'typical subjects' (People Management, Scaling-up, Digital Transformation, Management and Design) are actually offered, 'up to a maximum of 3 courses', so one of the four is dropped every year. PART-TIME ENROLMENT is available but is chosen after enrolment, in October, not at application. Also offered: exchange programmes with partner universities worldwide, an employer network for internships, peer tutoring for first-year students, and an annual entrepreneurial-ecosystem field trip.
english_only_accessibility: OPEN — one of the genuinely English-accessible unibz programmes. The only language requirement is English at B2; there is no Italian or German requirement at entry, during the studies, or for graduation. A candidate who speaks only English faces no language barrier at all. This is the decisive contrast with unibz's trilingual bachelors, where B2 in two of three languages is eliminatory and where the exit requirement is C1/C1/B1. Empirical check on how binding the language filter is here: neither of the two published 2026/27 ranking lists records a single exclusion on language grounds — the only exclusions itemised in the Early Bird list are two applicants who fell below the 70-point minimum score (69.35 and 67.09). The real constraints on this programme are therefore not linguistic but (a) the 12-ECTS curricular prerequisite for candidates without an economics/business bachelor, (b) the 70/100 minimum score, and (c) for non-EU applicants living abroad, the very small quota of 10 places against 28 ranked competitors.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with a merit-based ranking list decided entirely on DOCUMENTS — there is no written entrance exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT/GRE and no interview at any stage. Selection is a 100-point rubric with two components only: grade average (max 70 points) and a written START-UP PROJECT (max 30 points), plus a possible +2 for a bachelor awarded summa cum laude. A HARD FLOOR applies: a candidate scoring below 70 points in total is not merely ranked low but excluded from the ranking list entirely and must re-apply in a later session. Separate ranking lists are drawn for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad. English B2 is an eliminatory prerequisite that carries no points. Completeness is itself eliminatory: 'Only applications containing all requested documents will be evaluated. If one of the documents requested for criteria 1 and/or 2 is missing, you will not be considered for the ranking.' What makes this programme structurally different from every other unibz master is that a THIRD of the admission score is a creative deliverable rather than a measure of past academic performance — a strong start-up idea can lift a mediocre transcript over the line, and a strong transcript with a weak or missing project cannot pass.
academic_requirements: One of two routes. ROUTE 1 — a bachelor degree in one of these Italian degree classes or an equivalent qualification gained abroad: under D. 270/04, L-18 Economics and Business Administration or L-33 Economics; under D. 509/99, class 17 Economics and Business Administration or class 28 Economic Sciences; or a final degree or university certificate from an Italian School of Economics under the regulation in force before M.D. 509/99. Footnote: 'Italian citizen who have obtained their degree abroad must also have a secondary school leaving qualification.' ROUTE 2 — a bachelor in ANY other degree class (or equivalent gained abroad) provided AT LEAST 12 CREDIT POINTS were acquired in one or more of five subject areas: Business Administration, Economics, Law, Statistics-Mathematics, Technology and Engineering. The admission document enumerates the exact eligible SSD sectors with both post-2024-reform codes and legacy equivalents. BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION: AGRI-01/A (ex AGR/01), ECON-06/A (ex SECS-P/07) Accounting, ECON-07/A (ex SECS-P/08) Strategic Management, ECON-09/A (ex SECS-P/09) Corporate Finance, ECON-08/A (ex SECS-P/10) Business Organisation, ECON-09/B (ex SECS-P/11), IEGE-01/A (ex ING-IND/35) Management Science. ECONOMICS: AGRI-01/A (ex AGR/01), ECON-01/A (ex SECS-P/01), ECON-02/A (ex SECS-P/02), ECON-03/A (ex SECS-P/03), STEC-01/A (ex SECS-P/04), ECON-05/A (ex SECS-P/05) Econometrics, ECON-04/A (ex SECS-P/06), STEC-01/B (ex SECS-P/12). LAW: GIUR-01/A (ex IUS/01), GIUR-11/A (ex IUS/02), GIUR-03/B (ex IUS/03), GIUR-02/A (ex IUS/04), GIUR-03/A (ex IUS/05), GIUR-04/A (ex IUS/07), GIUR-05/A (ex IUS/08 e IUS/09), GIUR-06/A (ex IUS/10 e IUS/09), GIUR-08/A (ex IUS/12), GIUR-10/A (ex IUS/14), GIUR-11/B (ex IUS/21). MATHEMATICS AND STATISTICS: STAT-01/A (ex SECS-S/01), STAT-01/B (ex SECS-S/02), STAT-02/A (ex SECS-S/03), STAT-03/B (ex SECS-S/05), STAT-04/A (ex SECS-S/06), MATH-01/A (ex MAT/01), MATH-02/A (ex MAT/02), MATH-02/B (ex MAT/03), MATH-03/A (ex MAT/05), MATH-03/B (ex MAT/06), MATH-06/A (ex MAT/09), INFO-01/A (ex INF/01) Computer Science. TECHNOLOGICAL AND ENGINEERING: CEAR-08/D (ex ICAR/13) Industrial design, CEAR-10/A (ex ICAR/17) Drawing, IIND-02/A (ex ING-IND/13), IIND-03/A (ex ING-IND/14), IIND-03/B (ex ING-IND/15), IIND-04/A (ex ING-IND/16), IIND-05/A (ex ING-IND/17), IMAT-01/A (ex ING-IND/22), IEGE-01/A (ex ING-IND/35), IINF-05/A (ex ING-INF/05), INFO-01/A (ex INF/01). The breadth of Route 2 is the point: a computer-science, industrial-design, mechanical-engineering or law graduate can qualify on 12 ECTS alone, so this is one of the most discipline-open masters at unibz. TWO TRAPS, both stated explicitly: 'Courses included in the study plan of the Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation are not valid for the acquisition of the 12 ECTS required for the participation in the selection procedure as curricular requirements' (you cannot bootstrap the prerequisite from single-subject courses in this same master), and 'Courses that have been taken into consideration in order to achieve the above-mentioned 12 ECTS cannot be recognised for a possible career abbreviation' (spending credits on the entry gate forfeits them for credit recognition later). NOT-YET-GRADUATED THRESHOLD: at least 140 ECTS — notably HIGHER than the 120-ECTS standard used by most unibz masters, and a real filter on final-year applicants. At enrolment a foreign degree must be shown to carry at least 180 ECTS and to give access to a master programme. National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes, not in the same class (not LM-77/LM-77) and differing in at least 2/3 of course contents. The Faculty 'reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the single courses and/or teaching hours where necessary', so for foreign transcripts the content, not the title, decides.
entry_exam_or_test: NO entrance examination of any kind — no unibz aptitude test, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT, no GRE, no mathematics test and no interview. Admission is decided purely on the uploaded dossier. The only examination-type events connected to admission are the unibz LANGUAGE CENTRE ENGLISH EXAMS, and only for applicants who choose that route to prove B2. This programme's admission document labels them 'Language exams (online)', so they are sat remotely: EARLY BIRD — 16/03/2026 (registration 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration 24/03 - 08/04/2026); LATE — 22 - 26/06/2026 (registration 28/05 - 15/06/2026). CRITICAL GAP: NO unibz language exam session is offered for the Additional Application Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026), so an applicant entering in that window must already hold an external recognised certificate (LanguageCert, IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, etc.) or qualify through an English-medium high school or degree. Registration is done inside the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after an application has been created; if you start your application outside a registration period you must return to the portal during one of the listed periods. Separately, optional non-selective pre-courses run 21/09 - 09/10/2026 and intensive language courses 01 - 18/09/2026 for enrolled students; neither is an admission test.
selection_scoring: A 100-POINT RUBRIC WITH A 70-POINT FLOOR — the most distinctive scoring design at unibz, because 30% of the score is a creative submission. CRITERION 1, GRADE AVERAGE, MAX 70 POINTS: if already graduated, the final grade expressed in thirtieths; if not yet graduated, the grade average of university exams passed, expressed in thirtieths (and at least 140 ECTS must be declared). 'In the case of a bachelor concluded with the highest grade and the mention "summa cum laude", 2 additional points will be awarded.' CRITERION 2, START-UP PROJECT, MAX 30 POINTS, judged on four criteria: originality of the idea; coherence of the idea in the presentation (coherence in the content and development of the different elements); impact of the idea in terms of change (e.g. social impact, job creation); development of the idea (e.g. assessment of the problem/solution, creation of a prototype). CRITERION 3, MINIMUM SCORE: 'Minimum score to be admitted to the ranking: min. 70 points. This minimum score is the sum of the scores achieved for criteria 1 and 2.' Falling below 70 means exclusion from the ranking list, not a low rank — the Early Bird list names two applicants excluded on exactly this ground, at 69.35 and 67.09. TIE-BREAK: 'According to Art. 26, Paragraph 2), letter b) of the current admission regulation, in the event of equal scores, priority will be given to the applicant who has obtained a higher partial score for the more heavily weighted evaluation criterion' — i.e. the grade average — 'If scores are still equal, the younger applicant will have priority.' The signed ranking lists render the same rule as 'priority will be given to the applicant who has obtained the highest score for the first criterion'. ACTUAL 2026/27 CUT-OFFS, the single most useful planning datum for an applicant: EU EARLY BIRD — 30 admitted, top score 91.50, LOWEST ADMITTED 70.20 (i.e. effectively anyone clearing the 70-point floor was admitted); EU LATE — 18 admitted, top score 93.36, lowest admitted 70.50 (again essentially the floor); NON-EU LIVING ABROAD — 10 admitted, top score 88.77, LOWEST ADMITTED 80.23, with a waiting list of a further 18 ranked candidates running down to 70.30. The non-EU bar therefore sat roughly TEN POINTS above the EU bar. Read against the rubric, a non-EU applicant needed something close to a first-class transcript plus a well-developed start-up project, whereas an EU or parity-status applicant needed only to clear the formal floor. [uncertain] — note that scores are published to two decimals and range continuously, which implies a proportional conversion from the thirtieths grade into the 70-point scale, but unibz does not publish that conversion formula, nor any per-criterion breakdown of the 30 project points; the rubric's totals are certain, the internal arithmetic is not.
bonus_points: Two things function as score-boosters, and neither is the Webometrics or GMAT/GRE mechanism used elsewhere at unibz. (1) THE SUMMA CUM LAUDE BONUS: '+2 additional points' for a bachelor concluded with the highest grade and the mention "summa cum laude" (110 e lode in the Italian system, or the local equivalent). This is the only formally labelled bonus in the rubric and is worth 2% of the 100-point scale — enough to matter only at the margin. (2) THE START-UP PROJECT, worth up to 30 POINTS. Kerem's research brief frames this as a bonus and it is the field's headline number, but the official text treats it as CRITERION 2 of two — it is not an optional add-on that can be skipped. Omitting it is not a forfeit of 30 points but outright exclusion: 'If one of the documents requested for criteria 1 and/or 2 is missing, you will not be considered for the ranking.' Understood correctly, then, the 30 points are a mandatory component that behaves like a bonus in one specific sense: because the grade average is capped at 70 and the floor is also 70, a candidate with a perfect transcript still cannot be admitted on grades alone if the project scores zero, and conversely a candidate with a mid-range transcript reaches the floor only by scoring well on the project. WHAT IS ABSENT, for contrast with sibling programmes: no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that belongs to Software Engineering and Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance), no CV score (Software Engineering), no extracurricular-activities points, no portfolio or video scoring, and no interview points.
portfolio_and_materials: The START-UP PROJECT is the centrepiece deliverable and unibz publishes unusually candid guidance on it, in a 10-page slide deck by the then Degree Course Director Prof. Alessandro Narduzzo (Open Day 2022) linked directly from the admission section, plus a linked video. WHAT IT IS: a written description of an idea for a new and innovative enterprise. The NABC model developed at the Stanford Research Institute (Curtis Carlson and William Wilmot, 'Innovation - The Five Disciplines for Creating What Customers Want', 2006) is RECOMMENDED but explicitly not compulsory: 'Q3: Can I describe my innovative idea without using NABC? Yes, of course. We suggest this template, but this its use is not mandatory. If you have already developed your idea using another template, this is also fine.' The four NABC prompts are: what is the important customer and market NEED; what is the unique APPROACH for addressing this need; what are the specific BENEFITS per costs that result from this approach; how are the benefits per costs superior to the COMPETITION's and the alternatives. FORMAT AND LENGTH — note that unibz deliberately publishes NO hard limit, in contrast to the strict caps used by other unibz programmes (20 MB portfolio, 2 A4 project proposal, 6,000-character motivation letter, 2-minute video): 'Q5: the size: how many pages is allowed for the NABC? We deliberately did not set a rule: long enough to provide some rich context and elaborate some reasoning. For this purpose, at least 4 pages, I would say.' FILE FORMAT: 'Q7: the format: PDF, PPT, or WORD? A: pdf is certainly a preferred format.' LANGUAGE: 'You may write your document in English.' SUPPORTING MATERIAL: 'Q6: I already develop a prototype and a business model of my idea. Can I describe them in my document? Yes, you can describe them in the Approach section. If you produced video or other materials you think are relevant, please add the URLs of the external links' — so video is allowed as a linked extra, never as the submission itself. TWO STRATEGIC WARNINGS FROM THE FACULTY: on reusing an existing venture — 'Q1: I have already founded a startup. Can I use this idea for my application? In principle, you can; in practice, we do not recommend to do it. Unless, your idea is striving and highly original, and you expect to make an impact'; and on derivative ideas — 'Please, avoid to propose versions of existing ideas, adapted to a local market or to a segment of customers.' Social innovation is expressly welcomed: 'Q4 ... Social innovation is absolutely welcome, and any contextualization is appropriate. Still, do not forget the criteria to evaluate your idea are the same: originality, coherence, impact, development.' The closing instruction to applicants is attitudinal as much as technical: 'Convince us that you have the right mindset and the proper attitude to attend successfully this study program.' THE OTHER MANDATORY UPLOAD is the structured EXCEL FILE available in the application portal, used to declare the study career (and, for non-graduates, the ≥140 ECTS achieved). NOT required and not accepted for scoring: motivation letter, curriculum vitae, reference letters, design portfolio, standalone video.
interview: NONE. There is no interview at any point in the admission procedure — not as a standard stage, not as a conditional fallback for low-scoring candidates, and not for foreign-qualification verification. The admission document contains no interview section, the two signed 2026/27 ranking lists publish no interview dates, and no interview appears in the admission criteria (which comprise only grade average, start-up project and the 70-point minimum). This is a substantive difference from sibling unibz masters: the Master in Software Engineering routes sub-24/30 candidates to a CV evaluation and then an online interview, and the Master in Computing for Data Science holds published interview dates for below-threshold applicants. Here, the written start-up project performs the function an interview performs elsewhere — it is the qualitative, judgement-based component of the file — which means the applicant gets exactly one shot to make a personal impression and it is entirely on paper.
conditional_admission: Several distinct conditional regimes, and one threshold that is higher than the unibz norm. (1) NOT YET GRADUATED AT APPLICATION — 140 ECTS, NOT 120: 'If you have not yet graduated at the time of application: You can apply if you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS). In this case, you will be admitted conditionally, and you need to submit your diploma by the enrolment deadline.' The 140-ECTS bar is the same one used by the Master in Data Analytics and is 20 credits above the 120 used by most unibz masters — a final-year candidate with, say, 130 ECTS is not eligible here even though they would be for Software Engineering. The declaration is made via the portal's Excel file, and applicants graduating abroad must also upload a transcript of records in Italian, German or English plus the university's grading scale showing the minimum passing and maximum achievable final grade. In this situation the grade used for scoring is the average of exams passed, expressed in thirtieths, not a final degree grade. (2) THE DIPLOMA DEADLINE IS THE ENROLMENT DEADLINE: 13 October 2026, 12 midday. 'If you graduate after the enrolment deadline: You cannot enrol and you will lose your place, which will be offered to the subsequent applicant in the ranking list. In this case. you should not pay the tuition fees to secure your admission. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there still are available places, you can enrol by 11 December 2026.' (3) HOW COMMON IT IS IN PRACTICE — provisional admission is the norm rather than the exception on this programme: in the 2026/27 Early Bird EU list, 13 of the 30 admitted applicants carry the asterisk marking an unfinished bachelor (ranks 2, 6, 9, 11, 13, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 23, 24 and 30); in the Late EU list, 5 of 18 (ranks 7, 10, 12, 16, 17). (4) UNVERIFIED FOREIGN TITLES: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified', and admission stays 'under reservation' until the ARDI/CIMEA package is complete — 'If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' (5) ALL NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD are provisionally admitted regardless of their academic status: 'requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' (6) BACKSTOP: 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' Also stated: 'If you still need to graduate and/or certify the remaining exams you must sit, you are provisionally admitted in the ranking list.'
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE — there is no OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) regime for this programme. The admission document contains no OFA section and the two published ranking lists carry no OFA markings (the asterisks there denote provisional admission pending completion of the bachelor, not OFA). OFA at unibz is a bachelor-level instrument, applied where a compulsory mathematics test is failed (Bachelor in Economics and Management, Bachelor in Economics Politics and Ethics, Bachelor in Tourism Sport and Event Management) or where school mathematics grades score poorly (Bachelor in Computer Science). At master level the equivalent function is performed by the CURRICULAR PREREQUISITE — the 12 ECTS in Business Administration, Economics, Law, Statistics-Mathematics or Technology and Engineering — which must be satisfied BEFORE admission and cannot be remedied afterwards. Note in particular that the remedy route familiar from OFA is expressly closed here: courses in this master's own study plan do not count towards the 12 ECTS. The optional pre-courses running 21/09 - 09/10/2026 are a voluntary preparatory offering for incoming students, not an obligation.
language_requirements: Minimal and single-language: English at B2 (CEFR) to gain admission, and nothing else, ever. 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.' The requirement is ELIMINATORY — failure means exclusion from the admission procedure, not a lower rank — but it carries NO POINTS in the 100-point rubric, so there is no ranking advantage in holding a C1 or C2 certificate over a bare B2 (the only benefit of a higher level is safety margin against the lowest-sub-skill rule). No Italian, no German and no third language is required at admission, to sit examinations, or to graduate. Proof is uploaded in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or registered under 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'. A final certificate awarded by an Italian public institution requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original. Certificates that cannot be uploaded may be sent to the Language Centre by e-mail as PDF files or delivered in person, by the application deadline. Free Language Centre courses in German, Italian and other languages remain available to enrolled students as an option. Empirical severity check: neither published 2026/27 ranking list for this programme records any exclusion on language grounds — a striking contrast with unibz's trilingual bachelors, where language failures wipe out whole applicant groups.
entry_levels_by_position: Single-language pattern — 1st language English B2; no 2nd language; no 3rd language. In the schema's positional notation: 'B2 / none / none'. This is the simplest language profile available at unibz and materially easier than the B2/B2/none of the trilingual Bachelor in Computer Science or the C1/B2/none of the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance and the Master in Accounting and Finance — two Economics-faculty siblings which, despite sitting in the same faculty as this programme, demand a second language. Because there is only one teaching language, the usual unibz logic of ranking languages by the candidate's own strength does not apply: the requirement attaches to English specifically. Only B2-level exams can be registered for at the unibz Language Centre for this purpose ('Esame interno di livello B2' is the Language Centre entry in the recognised-certificates list); higher levels enter only through the recognition routes, where an English-medium high-school year or an English-taught degree is recognised as C1.
exit_levels: NONE — there is no language requirement to graduate from this programme. The admission document's 'Language requirements' section lists only 'Entry level (to gain admission)' and, unlike the trilingual programmes' documents, contains no 'Exit level (to graduate)' subsection at all. This is directly corroborated by the unibz Study Guide's dedicated page for students of English-taught masters, which addresses such students as being on a programme that 'is entirely in English and does not include language requirements in other languages' and frames Language Centre courses purely as an optional way 'to improve your language skills or learn a new language'. The contrast with the Study Guide's trilingual-master page is explicit: there, 'in order to graduate, you will need to certify two languages at the C1 level and the third language at the B1 level' — a rule that applies to trilingual masters and NOT to this one. The 120-ECTS study plan likewise contains no language course. A student admitted with English B2 can therefore complete the degree without ever raising a language level. CAUTION FOR RESEARCHERS: a naive search for 'unibz master exit language requirement' surfaces the trilingual page first and will wrongly suggest a C1/C1/B1 graduation gate for this programme.
third_language_exam_threshold: NOT APPLICABLE. The B1-in-the-third-language rule — under which a student must reach B1 before registering for the examinations of curricular courses taught in that language — exists only in unibz's trilingual programmes, where courses are delivered in German, Italian and English. This programme is taught entirely in English, so there is no second or third language in which examinations are held and consequently no threshold to meet, and no deadline attached to the first year's second semester.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways, all specific to English. (1) THE MAIN TEACHING LANGUAGE OF THE FINAL HIGH SCHOOL YEAR, if English — recognised as C1. For foreign qualifications, 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' (2) A BACHELOR OR MASTER DEGREE IN ENGLISH — recognised as C1. unibz graduates upload the certificates obtained and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); for foreign degrees, 'If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' This route matters more than usual here, because Route 2 of the entry requirements draws applicants from many disciplines and countries, a large share of whom hold English-taught bachelors. (3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official unibz list; 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' (4) LANGUAGE EXAMS ORGANISED BY THE UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE, taken ONLINE for this programme, registered through the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after filling out an application. Sessions and registration windows for 2026/27: Early Bird — 16/03/2026 (registration 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration 24/03 - 08/04/2026); Late — 22 - 26/06/2026 (registration 28/05 - 15/06/2026). 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' CRITICAL SESSION-SPECIFIC GAP: no unibz language exam session is listed for the Additional Application Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026), so an applicant using that window has only pathways 1, 2 or 3 available.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'), published trilingually. To be recognised, a certificate must (1) 'include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself' and (2) 'indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade (and/or the detailed assessment is indicated on the certificate itself or by appropriate documentation faithful to the original by the certification organisation)'. Further rules quoted from the resolution: 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed.' 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation.' 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list.' Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations are not accepted. Certificates of participation, end-of-course tests, examinations from private educational institutions and placement-test results are not recognised. Certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff are not recognised. 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.' VALIDITY: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January' — the Italian text clarifies that certificates issued from 1 January of the fifth preceding year onward remain valid for the whole of the current year. Items in the 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' section have unlimited validity. ENGLISH B2 THRESHOLDS FROM THE OFFICIAL TABLE, the practical detail an applicant needs: IELTS (Academic or General) 5.5 - 6.5; TOEFL iBT 72 - 94; Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, B2 First for Schools grade B or C, B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage) grade B or C (note grade A on any of these counts as C1, and a C1 Advanced result at level B2 also counts as B2); PTE Academic 59 - 75; PTE General Level 3; Pearson English International Certificate B2; LanguageCert General B2, LanguageCert Academic B2, LanguageCert ESOL B2 Communicator (4 skills); Trinity ISE II (B2); Aptis ESOL General B2 and Aptis ESOL Advanced B2; Michigan MET B2 in all 4 skills, and ECCE; TOEIC Listening 400+, Reading 385+, Speaking 160+, Writing 150+; Gatehouse Classic IESOL B2 and GATE B2; English Speaking Board ESB Level 1; unibz Language Centre 'Esame interno di livello B2'. HOME-EDITION EXCEPTIONS relevant to remote candidates: TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS, LanguageCert Academic, Classic IESOL and GATE are marked in the list as also accepted as 'home edition'. PRACTICAL WARNING: because the lowest sub-skill determines the level and there is no compensation, an IELTS with an overall 6.0 but a 5.0 writing band drops the applicant below B2 and triggers exclusion — the overall band alone is not enough. application_deadline_eu: Three sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. LATE APPLICATION (EU only): 28/05 - 08/07/2026 by noon local time = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September if places remain): 18/08 - 04/09/2026 by noon local time = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04. The Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation IS listed with the status '(Application possible)' on the Additional Application Session page for 2026/27, which is consistent with 48 of the 50 EU places having been allocated across the first two sessions. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and 'If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one' — a clause with real bite on this programme, since exclusion for scoring below 70 points is an explicit outcome and the two Early Bird casualties (69.35 and 67.09) were told they 'may re-apply in the second session'. All deadlines are 'by noon local time', i.e. a 12:00 CET cut-off, not end of day. AS OF THE VERIFICATION DATE (2026-08-29), the Additional Session is the only window still open and it closes on 2026-09-04.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application or the Additional Application Session, are ranked on a separate list against a separate 10-place quota, and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa. For this programme the single non-EU window is by far the most binding constraint in the whole record: it closed on 2026-04-28, only 10 places existed, the lowest admitted score was 80.23 against an EU floor of 70.20, and 18 further ranked candidates sat on a waiting list. As of the verification date (2026-08-29) no further non-EU intake for 2026/27 exists.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants — for this programme the difference between the two lists is worth roughly ten points of score, so classification matters more here than almost anywhere else at unibz. (1) Citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State. (2) Non-EU citizens with a valid Italian permit to stay under article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998 — 'permesso di soggiorno' for WORK, FAMILY reasons, POLITICAL or HUMANITARIAN ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. Such applicants 'apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay'; if the permit has expired a renewal request must be attached. 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid.' CRITICAL WARNING: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin', and the Early Bird ranking list restates it from the other direction: 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy ... you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.' WHAT PARITY IS WORTH ON THIS PROGRAMME, quantified from the 2026/27 lists: it moves a candidate from a list where 10 places were contested by 28 ranked applicants with a cut-off of 80.23, to a list where the cut-off was 70.20 in the Early Bird session and 70.50 in the Late session — i.e. essentially the formal minimum. It additionally unlocks the Late and Additional sessions (two extra chances) and removes the €50 application fee. For a Turkish applicant already living in Italy on a work or family permit, uploading that permit is the single highest-value action in the entire application.
places_quotas: Three separate quota figures for 2026/27. EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS GIVEN PARITY OF TREATMENT: Early Bird Application 40 places, Late Application 10 places — 50 EU in total. NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD: Early Bird Application 10 places, and no non-EU quota in any later session. The brochure summarises this as 'Places available: 50 EU + 10 non-EU', i.e. 60 places overall. CARRY-OVER RULE, for EU and parity applicants only: 'any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE. EU: 30 admitted in the Early Bird session against 40 places, then 18 admitted in the Late session — 48 EU admissions in total against 50 places, with the Late intake exceeding its nominal 10 because the 10 unfilled Early Bird places carried over (10 + 10 = 20 available, 18 admitted). This is why the Additional Session was opened despite the programme being popular. NON-EU: all 10 places filled, plus a WAITING LIST running from rank 11 to rank 28 — 18 further ranked candidates, i.e. 28 ranked applicants for 10 places, about 2.8 per place before counting anyone excluded outright for not meeting the requirements. Waiting-list candidates 'will be contacted by e-mail as of 6 June 2026 in case a spot opens up'. BOTTOM LINE: the EU door is wide (essentially anyone clearing 70 points was admitted in both sessions) and the non-EU door is narrow (10 places, a 80.23 cut-off, and a long queue behind it). Note also that the EU quota here (50) is one of the largest master quotas at unibz, while the non-EU quota (10) is one of the smallest — compare the Master in Software Engineering's symmetric 30 + 30.

This status will only be acquired upon enrolment' — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol, except for non-EU applicants abroad who fail to obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country. Appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Bozen-Bolzano Administrative Court within 60 days of notification or publication. required_documents: AT APPLICATION (online via the Application Portal, https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; the completed online form; and then the two exclusion-bearing dossiers. DOSSIER 1 — STUDY TITLE AND EXCEL FILE. If you graduated in Italy: the diploma supplement or a self-declaration under Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000 indicating the degree awarded and the exams passed. If you graduated abroad: the diploma supplement or final degree certificate with exams passed (the document must be written in Italian, German or English) AND a scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance, indicating the minimum final grade needed to obtain the qualification and the maximum final grade achievable, TOGETHER WITH the filled-in Excel file available in the application portal. In either case the document 'must contain the following information: final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian qualifications)'. If not yet graduated: declare at least 140 ECTS using the portal's Excel file, and if graduating abroad also upload the transcript of records in Italian, German or English plus the grading scale. 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the single courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' DOSSIER 2 — THE START-UP PROJECT (see portfolio_and_materials). Plus: English language proof under 'upload language certificates' and/or registration under 'enrol for language exams'; the diploma of a qualification already gained abroad (if not yet held, it is uploaded at enrolment); and for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay plus a renewal request if expired. THE COMPLETENESS RULE IS ABSOLUTE: 'Only applications containing all requested documents will be evaluated. If one of the documents requested for criteria 1 and/or 2 is missing, you will not be considered for the ranking.' Once submitted the application cannot be modified, and 'Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' The Admission Committee evaluates only documents uploaded by the application deadline. AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign university degree must upload: the bachelor degree diploma; an official translation of the degree into Italian (not necessary if issued in German or English); and the Diploma Supplement indicating both that at least 180 ECTS were achieved and that the qualification gives access to a master programme — plus the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements set out under credential_recognition. Non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit to the Student Office, in person or by e-mail, once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable ONLY by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. The admission document states: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' The university's page for non-EU applicants adds: 'The application fee is 50€. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.' EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons — pay no application fee. Because non-EU applicants abroad have only a single application window, the fee is a one-off rather than a per-session cost; an EU or parity applicant who uses all three windows still pays nothing.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year in two instalments: '1st instalment (€ 600): includes the revenue stamp of € 16. 2nd instalment (€ 600): must be paid by March of the following year.' The first instalment is the payment that secures an admitted place (deadlines 05/06, 06/08 or 25/09/2026 by noon depending on session); for continuing students the university fees page gives 1st instalment €600 by 13 October 2026 and 2nd instalment €600 by 31 March 2027. Over the two-year programme that is roughly €2,400. Delayed payment of the second instalment incurs a fine (€30) and automatically blocks the online account, meaning no access to mySNS, no exam registration and no transfer to another university or programme. No refund if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. FUORI CORSO: exceeding the normal length of the programme changes the status to 'fuori corso'; from the second year after the normal length the 1st instalment rises to €900, and from the second fuori corso year a €300 surcharge applies. EXEMPTIONS: students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law no. 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (health-authority certificate to be handed in by the first-instalment deadline — only the €16 revenue stamp is then payable), and foreign students granted a scholarship from the Italian government (total exemption on request, €16 stamp only). Students awarded a scholarship by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of the tuition fees paid for the academic year, typically reimbursed by unibz between March and April; late-payment fines are not reimbursed. Payment is made with the pagoPA payment slip. General fees page: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/
scholarships_grants: The main route is the income-based provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, administered by the Office for the Right to Study / Office for Higher Education Support and applied for online through the provincial e-government service, with form-filling assistance from the South Tyrolean Students Association (ASUS). Three instruments exist: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants for fostering postgraduate studies. Grant holders also receive reimbursement of the tuition fees paid for the academic year (reimbursed by unibz typically between March and April, after the provincial office notifies the university of recipients between February and March; fines for late payment are not reimbursed). CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — so a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is effectively ineligible in year one, and on a two-year master the grant is realistically available only for the second year. Other listed routes: grants from the Italian Government (via Italian embassies, consulates and Cultural Institutes — these also carry full unibz fee exemption), national schemes for Austrian and German students (BAföG), and loans from Italian banks. unibz itself grants fee exemptions rather than cash scholarships. NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC SCHOLARSHIP is published for the Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation; note in particular that despite the start-up orientation, no start-up or venture prize, incubator stipend or NOI Techpark grant is advertised as part of admission. credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign university degree must upload the bachelor degree diploma, an official translation into Italian (not necessary if the documents were issued in German or English), and the Diploma Supplement indicating both that at least 180 credit points (ECTS) were achieved and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. Then, depending on the education system: (a) EU COUNTRIES, SWITZERLAND, NORWAY, ICELAND, LIECHTENSTEIN — a Statement of Correspondence of the bachelor degree, downloaded from ARDI, the Automatic Recognition Database Italy (https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA, the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence; (c) NON-EU COUNTRIES NOT SIGNATORIES OF THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification. 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' unibz also warns that 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment'. DISTINCT FROM TITLE RECOGNITION, and specific to this programme, is the CURRICULAR check for Route 2 candidates: the 12 ECTS in Business Administration, Economics, Law, Statistics-Mathematics or Technology and Engineering must be evidenced from the transcript, which is why the Excel study-career file, the transcript in Italian/German/English and the grading scale are exclusion-bearing documents, and why 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the single courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' Recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to unibz courses — and expressly NOT for the courses used to satisfy the 12-ECTS entry requirement. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only, 02/03 - 28/04/2026 (€50 non-refundable fee) → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (10 places; 2026/27 cut-off 80.23; waiting list to rank 28 contacted from 6 June 2026) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → THEN start the visa application by pre-enrolling on the Universitaly portal of the Italian Ministry of Universities and Research. 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only', and the ranking list adds the sharper formulation: 'Should you not follow this procedure, your direct online application to unibz will be declared null and void.' The Italian diplomatic-consular authorities in the applicant's country then issue the entry visa for studies/university. Three explicit disclaimers apply: 'the application at unibz does not guarantee an appointment at the diplomatic-consular Italian representation'; 'the admission to unibz does not confer automatically any right to obtaining a visa'; and 'obtaining a study visa issued by the competent diplomatic-consular representation does not automatically confer any right to enrolment at unibz'. All non-EU citizens living abroad are only provisionally admitted, the requirement being 'the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz'. FINANCIAL MEANS: 'you will need at least € 800 per month for living (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) in the Bozen-Bolzano area', and unibz states that 'a master programme will cost € 24,000' in living costs over its duration, on top of the ca. €1,200 per year tuition; health insurance and visa expenses are budgeted separately. AFTER ARRIVAL: 'within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, according to Italian law you must apply for a residence permit' — contact the Advisory Service / Student Support immediately on arrival — and once the permesso di soggiorno is obtained a copy must be handed in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. WORK: 'no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year' — worth flagging on this programme in particular, because five components carry compulsory 75% attendance and the Project LAB and field trip add further presence requirements, so a heavy work schedule is hard to combine with the curriculum. REFUND EXCEPTION: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country are entitled to a refund. uncertainty_notes: Data year: all figures are for academic year 2026/27; the admission-information PDF carries 'Latest update: 24.08.2026' and the express caveat 'Subject to change.' Verified 2026-08-29. TIMING STATUS AT VERIFICATION: the Early Bird and Late sessions have CLOSED and both ranking lists are published; only the Additional Application Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026, EU citizens only) is still open, and this programme is listed as accepting applications in it — it closes in six days. The non-EU window for 2026/27 closed on 2026-04-28 and cannot be reopened. (1) STALE COVER YEAR ON BOTH PROGRAMME PDFs: the admission-information PDF and the brochure are both headed '2025/26' while every date inside them belongs to a.y. 2026/27 (application March-April 2026, ranking lists May-September 2026, classes 28/09/2026, exam sessions into 2027) and the footer is stamped 24.08.2026. Cross-checked against the sibling Economics-faculty documents for Data Analytics, Accounting and Finance and Public Policy, all of which correctly read '2026/27' — so this is a labelling error on these two files, not an older edition. Anyone quoting the cover year will misdate the whole record. (2) THE GRADE-TO-POINTS CONVERSION IS NOT PUBLISHED. The rubric says the grade average, expressed in thirtieths, is worth up to 70 points, but no formula or table is given for converting, say, 27/30 into a number of points. The published scores run continuously to two decimals (70.20, 79.88, 91.50), which implies a proportional mapping rather than bands, but a candidate cannot compute their own likely score in advance. This is the single biggest gap in the otherwise very explicit rubric. (3) NOR IS THE START-UP PROJECT RUBRIC WEIGHTED. Four evaluation criteria are named (originality, coherence, impact, development) but no per-criterion point allocation within the 30 points is published, and no scoring band descriptors exist. Combined with (2), it is impossible to reverse-engineer an admitted candidate's grade/project split from a published total. (4) NEITHER RANKING LIST CARRIES AN EXPLICIT SIGNATURE DATE — both read 'Bozen-Bolzano, date of the signature' with a digital-signature block, so only the scheduled publication dates (by 27/05/2026 and by 30/07/2026) can be cited. This differs from other unibz faculties, whose lists print the signing date. (5) COPY-PASTE ERROR IN BOTH RANKING LISTS: the simultaneous-enrolment paragraph in both PDFs reads 'the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-18/LM-18' — LM-18 is the computer-science class and belongs to the Engineering templates. The admission-information PDF correctly uses LM-77/LM-77. The rule is the same either way; only the example is wrong. (6) THE 30-POINT PROJECT IS NOT OPTIONAL, despite being framed as a bonus in some secondary summaries: the official text makes it criterion 2 of two, and omitting it causes exclusion from the ranking, not merely a 30-point loss. This record treats it accordingly. (7) SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS are not confirmed for 2026/27 — the €1,680-€6,960 range and any merit-average threshold come from secondary summaries, not from any page verified for this programme; the provincial call sets amounts annually. (8) No separate call/manifesto or Rector's decree was found in English for 2026/27; the most recent published Study Manifestos for this LM-77 programme are from 2015, 2016 and 2019 and are curricularly out of date, and the 'current admission regulation' cited in Art. 26 was not located in English. (9) ADDITIONAL SESSION QUOTA: the additional-session page confirms the programme is open but does not publish the number of remaining places; residual EU capacity is inferable as roughly 2 (50 EU places minus 48 admitted) plus any admitted candidates who failed to secure or enrol, but is not officially stated and could be materially larger if drop-off was high. (10) THE 30 EARLY BIRD EU ADMISSIONS AGAINST 40 PLACES do not necessarily mean only 30 qualified applicants: the list records only two named exclusions for scoring below 70 and refers generically to 'Applicants not included in the ranking list ... because they did not meet the admission requirements', whose number is not published. The same applies to the non-EU list. So the ratios reported here (2.8 ranked non-EU candidates per place) are floors, not true application-to-place ratios — the total number of applications received is nowhere disclosed. (11) TURKISH-APPLICANT RELEVANCE: Türkiye is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so case (b) recognition applies (ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification); this classification is inferred from the convention's membership, not stated by unibz for this programme. (12) STREAM NAMING IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS OFFICIAL SOURCES: the brochure and programme page call the second stream 'Innovation and Management', while the downloadable study-plan diagram labels it 'INNOVATION MANAGEMENT'. There is also a course named 'Innovation Management' inside the plan, which is a different thing from the stream. (13) THE NABC GUIDANCE DECK IS DATED 'Open Day 2022' and is signed by Prof. Alessandro Narduzzo as Director of the programme, whereas the current Degree Course Director is Prof. Christoph Stöckmann. The document is still the officially linked guidance and its FAQ answers are still the only published statement on length and format, but a cautious applicant should treat the '4 pages' figure as guidance rather than a rule and may wish to confirm with the Faculty Secretariat. (14) EXIT LANGUAGE LEVEL: the finding that there is NO graduation language requirement rests on two mutually supporting sources — the admission PDF's Language requirements section lists only an entry level, in structural contrast to the trilingual programmes' documents which carry an explicit exit subsection, and the Study Guide's page for English-taught masters describes such programmes as not including language requirements in other languages. It is a well-supported conclusion rather than a directly quoted 'there is no exit requirement' statement for this specific degree. (15) The admission PDF ends its language section with the boilerplate line 'For information on studying in three languages also visit the following page', which is a template artefact and does not make this a trilingual programme.
